data_payload.identification_strategy: Three-stage hierarchical procedure across multi-strain relaxation tests: Stage 1 fits the anchor segment (lowest strain in the linear viscoelastic threshold) to extract linear equilibrium modulus (Ge) and power-law transient constants (g1, n); Stage 2 fits subsequent non-linear relaxation curves with fixed linear constants to extract pointwise non-linear Helmholtz multipliers (he, h2); Stage 3 fits continuous candidate functions (Logarithmic vs Exponential) across the discrete Helmholtz multipliers to construct closed-form functions he(epsilon) and h2(epsilon).

constitutive_formulation.general_hereditary_integral: sigma(t, epsilon) = he(epsilon) * Ge * epsilon(t) + h1(epsilon) * int_0^t Delta_G(rho(t) - rho(tau)) * d[h2(epsilon) * epsilon(tau)] / dtau * dtau
constitutive_formulation.pure_relaxation_reduction: sigma(t, epsilon) = he(epsilon) * Ge * epsilon + h2(epsilon) * epsilon * Delta_G(t)
constitutive_formulation.reduced_time_simplification: rho(t) = t (shift factor a_sigma = 1 for isothermal soft tissue)
constitutive_formulation.relaxation_convention: h1(epsilon) = 1.0 (since h1 and h2 form a product in pure relaxation, h1 is fixed to unity while h2 captures the transient non-linear scaling)

stage_1_anchor_segment_fit.objective_function: min SSR_anchor = sum_{k=1}^{N_1} ( sigma_exp(t_k) - ( Ge * epsilon_1 + g_1 * t_k^(-n) * epsilon_1 ) )^2

parameters.name: EquilibriumModulus
parameters.physical_meaning: Linear equilibrium relaxation modulus at asymptotic long time.

parameters.name: TransientStiffness
parameters.physical_meaning: Transient relaxation stiffness coefficient scaling power-law decay.

parameters.name: PowerLawExponent
parameters.physical_meaning: Power-law time decay exponent governing the rate of transient relaxation.

stage_1_anchor_segment_fit.optimization_profile: CurveFitProfile.Automatic (routes to Standard / alglib.minbleic L-BFGS with box bounds)

stage_2_remaining_segments_fit.objective_function: min SSR_j = sum_{k=1}^{N_j} ( sigma_exp(t_k) - ( he * Ge* * epsilon_j + h2 * g_1* * t_k^(-n*) * epsilon_j ) )^2

parameters.name: EquilibriumHelmholtzMultiplier
parameters.physical_meaning: Strain-dependent non-linear multiplier scaling the equilibrium modulus.

parameters.name: TransientHelmholtzMultiplier
parameters.physical_meaning: Strain-dependent non-linear multiplier scaling the transient relaxation response.

stage_2_remaining_segments_fit.optimization_profile: CurveFitProfile.Automatic (routes to Standard / alglib.minbleic L-BFGS with box bounds)

candidate_functions.formula: y(epsilon) = a_0 + a_1 * epsilon + a_2 * epsilon^2 + ... + a_n * epsilon^n

stage_3_continuous_helmholtz_fitting.selection_criterion: Minimum FinalError (SSR) among successful candidate fits
stage_3_continuous_helmholtz_fitting.fallback: ConstantFunction when only a single strain segment is available

acceptance_test_verification.time_downsampling: Delta t >= 1.0 s between consecutive points (enforcing lower high-frequency noise and higher optimizer precision)

physical_deficiencies: Negative transient stiffness c < 0 produces anti-relaxing / unphysical behavior.
Negative exponent n < 0 inverts the power-law into an increasing function over time.
Degree-3 polynomials exhibit severe Runge oscillations between data points with non-monotonic artifacts.

output_summary: Validated and fully verified the Schapery Non-Linear 1D model curve fitting step (SchaperyRelaxationOnlyCurveFitterStep.cs) with real multi-strain ligament experimental data in AcceptanceTests. Enforced strict biomechanical physical validity ($G_e > 0, g_1 > 0, 0 < n < 1, h_e > 0, h_2 > 0$), resolving legacy unphysical negative constants and Runge polynomial artifacts from Populate_database.sql.
justification_for_decisions: Schapery's non-linear formulation separates the linear viscoelastic relaxation baseline from strain-dependent non-linearities via thermodynamic Helmholtz multipliers (he, h1, h2). In pure stress relaxation, fixing h1=1 and anchoring the initial segment to linear behavior (he=h1=h2=1) eliminates parameter coupling and ill-conditioning, enabling deterministic convergence via ALGLIB L-BFGS before fitting continuous candidate functions (Logarithmic vs Exponential).
